advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the aggregation guard verify observable behavior (e.g. execute the loop shape against a stub interpreter where one extra fails and assert non-zero exit + all iterations attempted) instead of grepping for the `rc=0`/`rc=1`/`continue`/`exit $rc` shell tokens.
evidence: `for shape in ("rc=0", "rc=1", "continue", "exit $rc"): assert shape in run` (test_ci_workflow_parity.py:265-271) greps the shell text of the step under test

These are shell IMPLEMENTATION idioms, not canonical identifiers a non-human consumer branches on (contrast the valid Rule-5 greps in the same file for job names / `_REUSABLE_BAT` workflow paths / `scripts/*.py` signatures that GitHub/CI actually reads)
Litmus (Rule 4): the assertion breaks on a behavior-preserving accumulator refactor with no observable-behavior change → change-detector

Regression blindness: the workflow is never run in-test; the substring `exit $rc` being present does not prove a failing extra sets `rc=1` and propagates — an `if ! { ... }` restructure that swallows the failure keeps all four tokens and passes
advisory.finding: `test_optionality_loop_aggregates_failures_and_never_activates` asserts by substring-grepping the loop step's shell SOURCE text for control-flow idioms (`rc=0`, `rc=1`, `continue`, `exit $rc`) rather than the observable failure-aggregation behavior. It is a change-detector: a behavior-preserving rewrite of the accumulator (e.g. `rc=$((rc+1))`, `((fail++))`, or extracting a helper) preserves the exit-nonzero-on-any-failure contract but drops the literal tokens and breaks the test; and because the loop is never executed, the test cannot detect an aggregation regression that leaves those literal tokens in place (e.g. an `if !`/`&&`-chain restructure that swallows a real failure).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that every interpreter/console-script invocation in the loop step uses an absolute `"$v/bin/..."` path (no bare `python`/`rebar-mcp` calls), covering the ticket's primary 'pass while testing nothing' footgun.
evidence: Workflow relies on absolute paths: `"$v/bin/python" -m pip install`, `"$v/bin/python" "$RUNNER_TEMP/check_extra.py"`, `"$v/bin/rebar-mcp" --help` (_optionality.yml:196-200)
Ticket ad63 acceptance criterion: 'Every interpreter/console-script call in the loop uses an absolute "$v/bin/..." path' — named as guarding a call that 'can pass while testing nothing'
Test 1 only asserts `"activate" not in run` (test_ci_workflow_parity.py:272); no assertion that interpreter/console-script invocations are absolute-path prefixed
Concrete failure path: rewriting `"$v/bin/python"` to `python` re-tests the ambient setup-python interpreter (extra never actually in it) and every existing guard still passes
advisory.finding: No test asserts the absolute-`"$v/bin/..."`-path invariant, which the ticket names as the #1 silent-failure footgun (a bare `python`/`rebar-mcp` runs the ambient interpreter and 'can pass while testing nothing'). `test_optionality_loop_aggregates_failures_and_never_activates` only checks the negative (`activate` absent); a regression that replaces `"$v/bin/python"` with bare `python` (or `"$v/bin/rebar-mcp"` with bare `rebar-mcp`) passes every guard while testing the wrong interpreter.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a checked-in test that parses infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json and asserts every required_status_checks context maps to a live workflow job name (and that no removed context — e.g. `extra "agents" installs`, `union [agents,eval,tracing] resolves` — remains), so the snapshot cannot silently re-stale on a future job rename.
evidence: `main-protection.snapshot.json` names the check context `{"context":"optional extras isolate (per-extra venvs + union)"}`, which must byte-match the workflow job `name:` at _optionality.yml:122.

rollback-mirror-lock.sh:82-85 POSTs the snapshot back verbatim ('recreating main-protection from snapshot' → `jq '{name,target,enforcement,conditions,rules,bypass_actors}' ... | api -X POST .../rulesets`), so a context that no longer maps to a real check would demand an impossible check on an emergency restore.

The new guards only assert loop-job existence and EXTRAS coverage; the test's own message instructs a HUMAN to fix the snapshot manually: 'Update _OPTIONALITY_LOOP_JOB (and infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json, which names the job's check context).' (test_ci_workflow_parity.py:240-241).

ABSENCE: `search_files('snapshot', 'tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py')` returned no matches — no test parses main-protection.snapshot.json or cross-checks its required_status_checks contexts against the reusable-workflow job names.
advisory.finding: The change relies on a manually-updated required_status_checks list inside the rollback snapshot, but adds no automated guard that the snapshot's contexts stay in sync with the live workflow job names — so a future rename of the `optional-extras` job will silently re-stale the snapshot and re-introduce the emergency-rollback-freezes-main hazard this change exists to fix.
scenarios: A later change renames the `optional-extras` job (or splits it) and updates _OPTIONALITY_LOOP_JOB but forgets the snapshot; CI stays green because no test asserts the snapshot content.
An emergency mirror-lock rollback then POSTs a required_status_checks context that no CI produces, and main is frozen — the exact failure mode this commit set out to prevent.
